stem:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
Assertion (A) : Most of the hot deserts of the world are located on the Western margins of continents between 15º-30º North and South latitudes.
Reason (R) : Trade winds lose their moisture and humidity as it move westward.
Codes :

options.label: a
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

expl: Most of the hot deserts of the world are located on the western margins of continents between 15º - 30º North and South Latitudes. Sahara and Kalahari deserts in Africa and Atacama in South America are examples. Trade winds towards this region reach from the Northern Hemisphere and Southern Hemispheres. Thus, upon reaching the western part of the continent, they turn dry. This causes very little rainfall in this region. It is an important factor for desert formation in this region. The reason, therefore, is the correct interpretation of the statement. Hence, option (a) is correct.

stem:
Statement (A) : Deserts can be effective sources for the production of perennial energy.
Reason (R) : As much energy is consumed by mankind in one year, Desert can receive the energy is more than that in only 6 hour from the Sun.
Choose the correct answer from the following code –

options.label: a
options.text: (A) and (R), both are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: b
options.text: (A) and (R), both are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

expl: Gerhard Knies, a German particle physicist, arrived at the remarkable conclusion that in just six hours, the world's deserts receive more energy from the sun than humans consume in a year. In this way, deserts can be a source of perennial energy. So, both the statement and reason are correct and the reason is the correct explanation of the statement.

stem: The probability of having a desert on the earth is more-
expl: The extension of hot dry desert climate on the earth is found between 15-300 latitudes. There are four major geographical conditions for the formation of deserts on the earth : (1) Presence of high air pressure around 300 latitudes. Here the winds keep descending from top to bottom, as a result of which the weather remains clear throughout the year. Sahara and Australian deserts come under this phenomenon. (2) The deserts of the western coast of the continents are found between 20-300 latitudes. Probably the reason for this is the eastern direction of the winds. Trade winds enter from the eastern part of the continents. By the time they reach the western part, they become dry. California (North America) W. Sahara (North Africa), Atacama (South America) and Namibia (South - West Africa) are similar deserts. (3) Among the desert located in the rain shadows region of the mountains, North American desert (Death Valley), Patagonia desert (Argentina) and Peruvian desert are prominent. (4) The deserts located in the middle of the continents, which are located away from the humid winds, include the Australian desert and the Gobi (China and Mongolia).

Code :

expl: Most of the Western and central interior region of Australia is arid and semi-arid (desert/semi-arid). About 70 percent of Australia is arid or semi-arid; therefore, Assertion (A) is correct. Northern Australia lies in the tropical regions; temperate regions are mainly found in southern Australia. Therefore, Reason (R) is not correct.

stem: The problem of desertification is least in which of the following continents?
expl: Europe is the only continent without a desert. Significantly, desertification is defined by the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) as "land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas (dryland) resulting from various factors, including climatic variations and human activities. Climatic variations include the decrease in precipitation, drought or soil and moisture loss on a global level. Notably, human activities include overgrazing, deforestation, removal of the natural vegetation cover and unsustainable agricultural activities in vulnerable ecosystems.

stem:
The Gobi Desert is spread across which of the following countries ?
1. Mongolia 2. China
3. Russia 4. Kazakhstan
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
expl: The Gobi Desert is a vast cold desert of Asia, mainly spread across southern Mongolia and northern China. Its extension does not reach Russia or Kazakhstan. The Altai Mountains lie to the north-west of this desert. Therefore, among the given options, the correct combination is only 1 (Mongolia) and 2 (China).

stem:
Consider the following deserts and arrange them in increasing order of their size (from smallest to largest)
(I) Great Sandy desert
(II) Arabian desert
(III) Sahara desert
(IV) Gobi desert
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
expl: The Great Sandy Desert is a desert in the northwest of Australia, mostly in Western Australia. It is the second-largest desert in Australia (after the Great Victoria Desert). It covers about 284,993 square kilometres (110,036 sq mi).Arabian Desert is a great desert region of extreme southwestern Asia that occupies almost the entire Arabian Peninsula. It is the largest desert area on the continent— covering an area of about 900,000 square miles (2,300,000 square km)—and the second largest on Earth, surpassed in size only by the Sahara, in northern Africa. Sahara Desert is the largest desert in the world, filling nearly all of northern Africa, it measures approximately 3,000 miles (4,800 km) from east to west and between 800 and 1,200 miles from north to south and has a total area of some 3,320,000 square miles (8,600,000 square km).Gobi, also called Gobi Desert, is a great desert and semi-desert region of Central Asia. The Gobi stretches across huge portions of both Mongolia and China. The Gobi occupies a vast arc of land 1,000 miles (1,600 km) long and 300 to 600 miles (500 to 1,000 km) wide, with an estimated area of 500,000 square miles (1,300,000 square km). Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

expl: Temperate desert is found between 300 to 600 latitudes. Deserts which come under the category of temperate deserts, are Gobi Desert, Ladakh Desert and Patagonia Desert.

stem:
Consider the following statements :-
(1) Tropical deserts in the world are found in the trade wind bands of western ends of Continents-
(2) In India, Eastern Himalayan region receives more rain from North-eastern winds.
Which among the above statements is/are/ correct ?
Code :
expl: Tropical hot deserts are often found in the region of trade wind band between 150 to 300 South or North of the Equator on the western side of continents. Therefore statement 1 is correct. In India, Eastern Himalayan region receives more rain from the southwest winds coming from the Bay of Bengal. Therefore, statement 2 is wrong.

stem: Which of the following deserts is located in the Southern Hemisphere?
expl: The Kalahari Desert is located in the Southern Hemisphere. It spreads over 930000 square km across (mainly) Botswana, Namibia and South Africa. The name of the desert comes from the Tswana word Kgala, which means "the great thirst" or "a waterless place".

stem:
What could be the main reason/reasons for the formation of African and Eurasian desert belt?
1. It is located in the sub-tropical high-pressure cells.
2. It is under the influence of warm ocean currents.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: Most desert regions are the result of large climatic patterns. The sub-tropical high-pressure belts are adiabatic in nature hence they bring little rainfall to the African and Eurasian desert regions. Warm ocean currents are not a necessary condition for the desert belt. For instance the, Gobi cold desert doesn’t come under the influence of any warm currents.

stem: Desert dwelling animals are called :
expl: Desert dwelling animals are called Xerocoles animals. Fossorial animals are those adapted to digging and life underground, while arboreal animals are those adapted to life in the trees and terrstrial animals are adapted to life on land.
